title: Was I Wrong About Tomb Raider: The Crypt of Chronos?
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WlQ0dZTiUNo

Daniel (@dungeondive) returns to Tomb Raider: The Crypt of Chronos to see whether his enthusiastic first review still holds up. The solo game was easy to relearn, and its tight scope still appeals to him. Setup and upkeep are manageable enough that the decisions on the board get most of his attention.

The randomized island campaign remains his favourite way to play. Lara moves between four environments, drawing dungeons with different objectives and special rules as she searches for the way to the final tomb. Daniel also revisits the dice pool that makes her choose how to spend her time, the crafting system that turns scavenged materials into gear and abilities, and the pleasure of using noise as a decoy while Lara stays hidden.

He has reservations about enemy line of sight and some of the tile art, particularly in the mountains. He finds the difficulty about right for his tastes, though he suggests starting with the advanced enemies if you already play hobby board games. More enemy variety and more ways to interact with the terrain top his wish list. He's also curious what the same system could do in a fantasy or science fiction setting while keeping the game compact.

----

If you could add one thing to the island campaign, would you choose more enemy variety, more ways to use the terrain, or something else?
